scope: mob_recon positive/negative controls through the production preflight guard, fixed 3.1.9 env + controlled 3.1.8 DB

inputs.positive: recon-positive.fasta = pUTI89 complete plasmid + the no-plasmid chromosome (69 contigs) sha256 80464c008171dde02ea731d3fe05806860783bb2511edfb84ad324a47f06817e

results.positive: exit 0; pUTI89 (114,230 bp) reconstructed as its own plasmid cluster AA337 and typed IncFIA+IncFIB/MOBF+MOBP/MPF_F — correct IncF profile; chromosome contigs remained chromosome
results.negative: exit 0; all large contigs chromosome, but 2 small contigs (NODE_51 4,965 bp + NODE_55 1,683 bp) assigned plasmid cluster AF232

boundary_observation: the AF232 assignment rests solely on mash nearest neighbor CP034740 (E. coli plasmid) at distance 0.0593303 — just under the native default cutoff — with zero biomarkers (rep/relaxase/mpf/orit all '-', non-mobilizable). Native mob_recon assigns biomarker-free small contigs to plasmid by mash proximity alone; this is upstream default behavior, not a pipeline defect, but downstream consumers must not treat mob_recon 'plasmid' labels on small biomarker-free contigs as strong evidence
consistency: AF232 content and mobtyper rows are byte-identical between the positive and negative runs (same 2 contigs, same mash evidence)
limits: software controls on two fixtures; not a sensitivity/specificity benchmark
mge.report/biomarker detail files retained but not independently re-derived
no cache-identity wiring, optional filter, OCI/platform acceptance
